## Natural history notes

A slender blister beetle characterized by its soft, elongated body, narrow head and thorax, and gray-brown to dark coloration with fine pale striping or banding. In Florida, it is found in open habitats such as fields, prairies, roadsides, gardens, agricultural edges, and other areas with herbaceous vegetation and flowers. Adults feed on leaves, flowers, and pollen, while the larvae are associated with grasshopper egg pods or other soil-dwelling insect eggs; like other blister beetles, it can produce cantharidin, a defensive chemical that may irritate skin if handled.
